LP-0MVLHMAWV008EKTI AC3 (delegated here) carries the completion verdict.

- LP-0MVLHMAWV008EKTI (restart-safe logging, on dev) guarantees the window is fully

3. Paste the measurement JSON + hourly table into LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2, and post the

data.description:
## Goal

Stop admitting local prefills that cannot possibly finish before the prefill deadline, and widen the deadline just enough to admit the largest genuinely feasible prompt:

1. **Cold-prefill admission budget = 25,000 tokens** of *new* (uncached / to-be-prefilled) tokens — a cap on what the GPU must actually compute, not on prompt size.
2. **`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`: 90 → 110 s**, so a feasible 25k prompt (~100 s at the measured 20–30k band rate) completes instead of being cancelled at 90 s.

## Why (measured on this host, 2026-10-24/25)

Prompt-eval rates from `llama-server` logs (268 samples), size-dependent with a knee at ~27k:

| Prompt | Median rate | Prefill |
|---|---|---|
| 10–20k | 281 t/s | 36–71 s |
| 20–30k | 249 t/s | 80–100 s |
| 30–40k | 181 t/s | 165–210 s |
| 48k | 152 t/s | ~320 s |
| 63k | 114 t/s | ~563 s |

Consequences measured in the 2026-10-24 18:38–23:47 window: **160 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events**, 45 local tasks cancelled mid-prefill, **~780k of ~840k prefill tokens computed then discarded (~93 % waste)**. A 38k cold prefill (~210 s) can never fit a 90 s deadline; 25k (~100 s) can fit 110 s with ~10 % margin.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Budget:** a configurable cold-prefill budget (`local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000`; 0 disables → rollback) caps the **new (prefilled) tokens** admitted for a local dispatch. Requests whose live-measured (or conservatively priced) new-token count exceeds the budget are refused at admission (skip local, chain detours), never dispatched and never cancelled at the deadline.
- **AC2 — Deadline:** `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 110`. Preserve the documented ordering `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds (60) < deadline (110) < local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds (840) < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds (900)` and keep the deadline strictly below the client's 900 s queue deadline. Add a config-load assertion for the ordering.
- **AC3 — Pricing:** budget comparison uses the measured prefill rate for the request's size band (or the existing p75 ETA percentile pricing, never the optimistic point estimate), so 25k at the 20–30k band is admissible and >25k cold is refused.
- **AC4 — Regression evidence:** over a 24 h window post-deploy, scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events are ≤10 % of the 2026-10-24 baseline (160 per 5.4 h), wasted-prefill tokens are correspondingly reduced, and there is no increase in client-visible 503 s / retries.
- **AC5 — Warm path unchanged:** warm requests (high `cached_ratio`, small `new_tokens`) remain admissible even when total prompt size exceeds 25k; assert no regression for the cached-append workload (e.g. 47k prompt / 549 new tokens stays local).
- **AC6 — Documentation + rollback:** config comments state units, interaction with `cold_threshold`/`warm_threshold`, the admission guard, and the rollback values (budget 0 / deadline 90).

## Tests

- Unit: budget boundary (24,999 admitted / 25,001 refused); warm bypass above 25k prompt size; deadline ordering guard rejects a violating config; budget pricing uses band rate, not point estimate.
- Integration: fixture replay of the 2026-10-24 thrash window → zero admitted cold prompts >25k; every refused request detours with a logged reason.

## Relationships

- discovered-from: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG (resident-prefix/tenancy admission). This item delivers the *budget* half of that item's AC3 ahead of the scheduler work and must ship independently; AC3 of LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG is to be re-scoped to the live-prefix pricing half when this lands.
- Do not increase the number of live slots in this item (per-slot ctx shrinks 131k → 87.4k at 3 slots).
data.title: Cold-prefill admission budget 25k tokens + prefill deadline 90s -> 110s

data.description:
## Goal

Evaluate (with measurements, go/no-go) whether widening the **per-session KV snapshot pool** (`session_slot_pool_size` 2 → 4, snapshots under `session_slot_save_path/slot_<id>.bin`) raises local prefix reuse for the small/medium working set — as the recommended alternative to adding live llama slots, which would shrink per-slot context (262,144 → 87,381 at 3 slots) and exclude the long-context sessions that dominate this workload.

## Why

- Measured prefix reuse is poor: aggregate 26.1 %, median **15.6 %** for prompts >20k tokens (227 prompts), 28 fully cold; 27 distinct sessions cycled through a 2-slot pool in ~5.4 h.
- More live slots buy *residency*, not throughput (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` serialises prefills), and cost per-slot address space for a long-context workload.
- The snapshot mechanism already exists (per-session save/restore, `session_slot_timeout_per_token_seconds: 0.0015`, capped at `session_slot_max_timeout_seconds: 60`, pool capped by `session_slot_pool_size: 2`) but is degraded under load (`session_slot_skip_when_busy: true`, circuit-breaker cooldown). Restore cost estimate: ~50k tokens ≈ 75 s → capped 60 s, so the mechanism currently helps only the <40k band.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Benchmark:** measure save/restore latency (and disk footprint) per prompt-size band (10k / 25k / 40k / 60k+) on the production GPU host, including under load (another session streaming), against the 0.0015 s/token timeout model.
- **AC2 — Go/no-go with evidence:** with `session_slot_pool_size: 4` in a replay/bake-off on the 2026-10-24 thrash window (or equivalent fixture), report the reuse uplift (baseline 15.6 % median for >20k prompts) and the restore-success rate (skip_when_busy / cooldown exclusions).
- **AC3 — If go:** ship the config change plus retention/eviction semantics for 4 snapshots (pool eviction policy, disk cap, failure cooldowns unchanged) and any report/observability fields (restore-hit rate per session, snapshot pool occupancy) so the proxy-usage-analysis report can monitor the effect.
- **AC4 — If no-go:** record the measured blockers (latency, skip rate, restore failures) as a comment on this item so the decision is reproducible.
- **AC5 — No change to live slot count or per-slot ctx in this item** (that remains the separate 3-slot "fast" profile discussion).

## Tests

Bake-off harness replaying fixture logs + real save/restore micro-benchmark on the host; unit tests for pool-size > 2 retention semantics; report-schema tests for the new fields.

## Relationships

- discovered-from: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG (slot-churn / tenancy investigation, option 3a of the recommendation).
- This is an evaluation/deliberation item, not a mandate to change configuration.
